package_info.package_manager: Manual/Custom deployment (malware distributed via CI/CD compromise, not a public package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: GraphicalProton is a backdoor deployed by threat actors after exploiting JetBrains TeamCity and Zabbix vulnerabilities. It enables persistent remote access, data exfiltration, and command execution, leveraging trusted cloud services for stealthy command-and-control. Its deployment subverts the software supply chain, allowing attackers to manipulate builds, steal sensitive assets, and maintain long-term unauthorized access to critical infrastructure.

execution_context.trigger: At Zabbix service startup (post-exploitation, after initial access to TeamCity/Zabbix server)
execution_context.file_location: Zabbix installation directory (malicious DLL side-loaded via DLL hijacking, replacing or masquerading as a legitimate Zabbix DLL)
required_permissions: filesystem (write access to application directory to place DLL)
code execution (to run DLL in Zabbix process context)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious DLL loaded via DLL hijacking, replacing or masquerading as a legitimate Zabbix DLL. The DLL loads at Zabbix service start and executes embedded backdoor logic.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At Zabbix service startup, the malicious DLL is loaded by the Zabbix process via DLL hijacking, executes embedded backdoor logic to establish persistence, initiates network communication for remote command execution, and enables data exfiltration, resulting in unauthorized remote access and control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL hijacking allows attackers to execute arbitrary code within a trusted process, bypassing security controls and evading detection. The presence of a non-standard DLL with backdoor logic in the Zabbix directory is highly anomalous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Zabbix DLLs should only contain expected monitoring or plugin logic and should not initiate network connections or provide remote access capabilities. Loading untrusted or modified DLLs from the application directory is not standard practice.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DLL side-loading may be used for legitimate plugin extension or debugging, but never for embedding backdoor logic or enabling remote command execution.
key_indicators: Unexpected or recently modified DLLs in Zabbix installation directory
DLLs with network communication or process injection code not present in official releases
Persistence via service auto-start with non-standard DLLs
Unsigned or improperly signed DLLs replacing legitimate binaries

execution_context.trigger: During runtime (after backdoor installation, on attacker command or scheduled interval)
execution_context.file_location: Memory (networking code executed by GraphicalProton backdoor process)
required_permissions: environment_vars (to access system or user context for exfiltration)
filesystem (to read files for exfiltration or staging data)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Outbound HTTPS requests to OneDrive or other trusted cloud services, used as command-and-control (C2) channels for exfiltration and receiving attacker instructions.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During runtime, the backdoor initiates outbound HTTPS connections to attacker-controlled OneDrive accounts, polls for commands, retrieves instructions, and exfiltrates collected data via encrypted payloads, resulting in covert remote control and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of trusted cloud services for C2 communications is a stealthy evasion technique, blending malicious traffic with legitimate business activity and bypassing traditional network security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Zabbix or TeamCity processes should not communicate with external cloud storage for command polling or data exfiltration. Outbound connections to personal or attacker-controlled cloud accounts are abnormal for server infrastructure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated backup or synchronization tools may use cloud storage, but do not poll for arbitrary commands or exfiltrate sensitive data to unapproved accounts.
key_indicators: Unusual OneDrive, Dropbox, or Google Drive traffic originating from server processes
Outbound HTTPS connections to cloud storage accounts not associated with business operations
Encrypted or obfuscated payloads in cloud storage uploads
Regular polling intervals to cloud services from non-user processes

execution_context.file_location: Memory (injected or executed by attacker via backdoor, targeting LSASS process)
required_permissions: filesystem (to drop or stage credential dumping tools)
process (to access and read LSASS memory)
privileged access (SYSTEM or Administrator rights required)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Execution of Mimikatz or similar credential dumping tool to extract Windows credentials and password hashes from memory.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining privileged access, the attacker executes Mimikatz to access LSASS process memory, extracts Windows credentials and password hashes, and stages them for exfiltration, enabling lateral movement and further privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Credential dumping is a hallmark of post-exploitation activity, used to expand attacker access within the network and compromise additional accounts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate processes should not access LSASS memory or extract credential material outside of controlled forensic or incident response scenarios. Such access is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensic or incident response teams may use credential dumping tools in controlled investigations, but never as part of normal server or CI/CD operations.
key_indicators: Mimikatz or similar credential dumping tool execution on production servers
Unauthorized access to LSASS process memory
Unusual process injection or memory read operations targeting credential stores
Creation of files or network activity containing credential data

attack_chain.action: Exploit CVE-2023-42793 in JetBrains TeamCity or Zabbix vulnerability to gain initial access to CI/CD or monitoring server.
Deploy GraphicalProton backdoor via DLL hijacking in Zabbix or direct installation on TeamCity server.
Establish outbound C2 channel using trusted cloud services (e.g., OneDrive) for command polling and data exfiltration.
Execute credential dumping tools (e.g., Mimikatz) to extract credentials and escalate privileges.
Use compromised CI/CD environment to manipulate builds, steal source code, signing certificates, or inject further malware into the software supply chain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Supply chain compromise and persistent access

behavioral_signatures: DLL hijacking in Zabbix or other monitoring tools, especially with non-standard or unsigned DLLs
Outbound HTTPS traffic to cloud storage services (e.g., OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive) from server processes not typically associated with such activity
Execution of credential dumping tools (Mimikatz or similar) on CI/CD or monitoring servers
Unusual process injection or memory access patterns targeting LSASS or other sensitive processes
Regular polling intervals to cloud services from non-interactive server accounts
file_indicators: Unexpected or recently modified DLLs in Zabbix or TeamCity directories
Modified, unsigned, or improperly signed DLLs replacing legitimate binaries
Presence of Mimikatz or similar credential dumping binaries or modules in server file systems
Files containing credential dumps or exfiltrated data staged for upload
network_indicators: Outbound connections to OneDrive, Dropbox, or other cloud storage from CI/CD or monitoring servers
Unusual encrypted traffic to cloud services not associated with normal business operations
Regular HTTPS requests to cloud storage APIs from server infrastructure
Connections to cloud accounts or endpoints not whitelisted for business use
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized or unexpected DLLs in application directories, especially those loaded by Zabbix or TeamCity processes. Alert on outbound HTTPS connections to cloud storage services from server infrastructure, focusing on traffic to accounts or endpoints not associated with business operations. Detect execution of credential dumping tools and unauthorized access to LSASS memory. Correlate privilege escalation and lateral movement with recent software or DLL changes on critical infrastructure. Implement file integrity monitoring and network anomaly detection to identify suspicious modifications and exfiltration attempts.
